items.title: Prints sticking to FEP and not the Print Plate
items.originalText: Prints sticking to FEP and not the Print Plate Hello. I have the Mage S 14K, it worked great for a while, but then prints started to not stick to the plate, and boy oh boy are they sticking to the FEP. The FEP became dented so I changed it out, and it worked fantastic for ONE print. And now nothing sticks again. I’ve done six prints all on different days, nothing sticks to the plate. I’ve setup multiple attempts small prints all over the plate, looking if it is just one area or something, nothing close to each other, and nothing sticks. Well, as stated it sure sticks to the FEP, real pain getting it to come off that, but the plate, nothing. I have no idea how to fix this, Looking at other posts I dont see any real answers? Can anyone help?

items.originalText: HALOT BOX is crashing Hello everyone. HALOT BOX has been crashing on me when I click RESIN to continue the slicing process. items.originalText: HALOT SKY 2022 – LCD does not display layer image even after screen replacement I am experiencing a serious issue with my Creality HALOT SKY 2022 resin printer. The printer turns on normally, the UV LEDs work, and the mirror is clean. However, the LCD does not display any layer image during printing, and the problem persists even after installing a brand new original 9.25’’ 6K mono LCD. Description of the problem: · During printing, the UV backlight turns on, but the LCD remains completely dark. · No layer pattern is projected on the LCD surface. · Running Clean Screen also produces the same result: the entire center area stays dark. Actions already taken: 1. Installed a brand new original LCD panel (9.25’’ 6K mono) specifically made for HALOT SKY 2022. But, no improvement. Please advise: 1. How to properly diagnose whether the issue is the LCD driver board or mainboard? 2. Do you have official replacement parts for the HALOT SKY 2022: · LCD driver board · Ribbon cable · Mainboard (if required) I can provide photos and videos if needed. Thank you in advance. Looking forward to your assistance.

items.title: K2 Series Flagship Printers - Bed Leveling and Maintenance
items.originalText: K2 Series Flagship Printers - Bed Leveling and Maintenance Bed Leveling: I’ve done a perfect bed leveling on my K2 Pro. There’s no need for extreme measures. I leveled the bed using the Paper Method, turning the knobs to perfection. I didn’t need sanding, aluminum tape, or anything else. It went from 0.45 to 0.25. Even when it was tilted, my printer was printing flawlessly. You can follow this official Creality video tutorial to perform your leveling, the leveling method starts at 6:24. You must fine-tune each corner at least four times in a circular pattern because when you fine-tune one knob, you mess with the level on the other side. Don’t forget to perform all calibrations after you leveled the bed. You can access the Fluidd web interface by entering the printer’s IP address in your internet browser, plus the door :4408 (example: http://192.168.1.3:4408/ ). Maintenance: I also recommend everybody to perform frequent maintenance on your printers, they will last longer and the printing results will be perfect. Apart from the normal maintenance you see in the video, I also recommend everybody to lubricate all the rollers on the printer frequently. For that, Creality recommends using only WD-40 Specialist Silicone spray. Check this official Creality video for maintenance tips. WD40 specialist Silicone spray 600×359 8.51 KB Levelling 2x 1920×2319 176 KB

items.title: Hello everyone
items.originalText: Hello everyone Hello Everyone! My name is Keagan Stephens, all the way from SA! I am 31 years old ,I Live in Eshowe Kwa-Zulu natal 3815 (ZULULAND!) and i Am a Qualified Post Basic Pharmacist Assistant And the owner of Sculptured Realities. My 3d printing Journey Started about 6months ago when i was trying to find a way to make a toy replica of my daughter and had asked a friend of mine whom if fortunate enough to own a Creality Ender KE. I Loved the results and got the cheapest 3d printer i could find which i still use today (easythreed k9 and k10). this was 5 months ago , since then I saved up to get a Creality Halot r6 WHICH WAS ON SALE AT THE TIME. I Really loved the quality prints i got from the Halot R6 and decided to open a business based around 3d Prints specifically aiming to make life like busts that resemble clients likeness, which has gone amazingly well especially since i’ve been unemployed for the past 2 years due to a major unemployment rate the country is facing . since starting i’ve been working with our local bakers trying to fill in the gap by bringing affordable cake toppers and baking related tools such as cookie cutters and stencils etc(we live in a remote area)..i am also currently working on fun kids theme pot planters ,lamps and articulated toys ,keychains and much more which i believe will get kids to get excited about 3d printing and nature as a whole. My future goals for myself and my company is to move on to larger life sized 3d printing aswell as move on to automotive 3d printing applications (mainly engine and interior trimming aswell as afew designer parts). items.title: Redémarrage Halot Lite
items.originalText: Redémarrage Halot Lite Bonjour, toutes mes dernières impressions n’ont pas tenue à la plaque ou ont été ratées (la résine s’est effondrée sur elle même - création au look “fondu”). je n’ai pu imprimer avec mon imprimante que 3 créations, dont une grosse. Suite à cela j’ai mis la machine de côté. Aujourd’hui j’ai besoin d’imprimer des éléments avec, pour mes enfants et moi. (une arme de robot, une plaque de jeu de société/plateau) Je cherche une personne qui n’habiterait pas trop loin afin de venir m’aider. c’est ma première imprimante 3D et je n’ai surement pas tout compris. je prépare les STL avec CHITUBOX. sculpturevictoria 1448×1086 140 KB j’ai testé plusieurs résines et je n’arrive plus à imprimer. je ne sais pas d’ou vient le problème. j’ai même remplacer le film protecteur de l’écran (je n’ai plus aucune pièce de rechange). sur le site de creality je ne vois aucune pièce détachée pour mon imprimante. lorsque ça imprime il y a de la résine partout sur la plaque de support… AIDEZ MOI SVP. MERCI.

items.title: Parts and service
items.originalText: Parts and service I don’t know where to send this, so I’ll drop it here, maybe someone is paying attention. First off The people of customer service are great, My issue is how to obtain not normally purchased parts. I got resin on the power distribution board of my Halot Mage S and it died. The fact that there is no dedicated site to purchase these parts is a good reason to look at other printers. One week to explain that it is my fault and get the info needed. I love the fact that they want to help, but I knew how it would end. The order process is this. Send money to this link via Paypal, and then send the invoice # back to them. Wait two-three days and they send a message saying that they have sent the invoice # to other people for verification of the invoice #, and then they will send the order to the people to ship it… Maybe. This is a convoluted mess that can be easily fixed by having a dedicated site. Just take my money and send the part. For a company that prides customer service, this is a huge fumble. Yes, I would have used ebay if they had any.

items.originalText: Printing Issue with Creality Halot Mage S 14K – One Side Prints Perfectly, the Other Doesn’t Hello everyone, I’m experiencing a recurring printing issue with my Creality Halot Mage S 14K , and I’d like to know if anyone else has encountered the same problem. As you can see in the photos, one part of the model prints perfectly, with all the details clearly reproduced, while the opposite side shows significant defects : incomplete printing, deformations, and areas where the resin doesn’t seem to have cured properly. This issue occurs with different models and two different resins : Fast Cast SuperCast (pink) Liqcreate Wax Castable (blue) I’ve already tried several prints, adjusting the exposure settings, model orientation, and support configurations, but haven’t been able to solve the problem. The printer is properly leveled, the workshop temperature is around 22°C (72°F), and the UV screen appears to be working correctly. What puzzles me most is that two opposite areas of the same model, printed simultaneously, show completely different results . Has anyone experienced this issue, particularly with this printer? Do you have any idea what might be causing it (UV screen, vat film, exposure settings, peeling forces, or something else)? And most importantly, has anyone found a solution? Thanks in advance for your help and advice!
